Ardā Wirāz Nāmag, chapter 1, from The Book of Arda Viraf: the Pahlavi text prepared by Destur Hoshangji Jamaspji Asa, revised and collated with further manuscripts by Martin Haug, assisted by E. W. West (Bombay and London, 1872), pp. 3–8, read from the Internet Archive scan (bookofardaviraf00haug). The § numbers are Haug's sentence numbers; later editions divide the chapter differently. Book Pahlavi script has no computer encoding of its own, so the script on the page is Haug's 1872 Pahlavi type itself, cut into words from the scan. Under it are the words as they were read aloud, in D. N. MacKenzie's transcription (the scholarly standard since 1971); the "As written" switch changes that line to the letters of the script in the usual transliteration, Aramaic word-signs in capitals. The print's sentence numbers and punctuation rings are left out of the images. The text is Haug's. Where his reading of a word has since been given up, the word is read as it is today and the note says so; where later editors correct the manuscripts, Haug's print is kept and the note gives the correction. Pronunciation: Middle Persian of the third century as MacKenzie reconstructs it. The translation is new, made from the Pahlavi. Still to do: the "As written" letters were set down from Haug's printed Pahlavi with the help of his own Roman reading of each word, and not every letter has yet been checked against the page.
